job.title: Transport Coordinator
job.description:
About the Role

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Transport Coordinator to join our clients team on a 9-month fixed-term contract. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced logistics environment, has a strong commitment to safety, and enjoys working collaboratively with both internal stakeholders and external transport providers.

The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting daily transport operations, ensuring processes are followed accurately, and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

The duties of this role include, but are not limited to:
  • Load restraint activities (full on-the-job training provided)
  • Load building activities (full on-the-job training provided)
  • Gate checks and compliance verification (full on-the-job training provided)
  • Scanning and management of delivery documentation
  • Administrative support and receptionist duties
  • Sorting and preparation of load packs
  • Archiving and document management
  • Supporting transport operations and coordinating with subcontractor drivers
  • Maintaining accurate records and ensuring compliance with operational procedures
About You

To be successful in this role, you will possess:
  • A strong commitment to workplace safety
  • Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills
  • A process-driven mindset with the ability to follow procedures consistently
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • The ability to build effective working relationships with internal teams and external subcontractors
  • A proactive approach to identifying and implementing continuous improvement opportunities
  • Competent computer and administrative skills
  • Previous experience in the transport, logistics, warehousing, or supply chain industry will be highly regarded
Working Hours

Standard Hours:
  • Monday to Friday
  • 10:00am – 6:00pm
Training Period:
  • Monday to Friday
  • 9:00am – 5:00pm
The successful candidate should be flexible and reliable during the training and onboarding period.

Why Join?
  • Opportunity to gain valuable experience within a transport and logistics operation
  • Comprehensive on-the-job training provided
  • Supportive team environment
  • Fixed-term role with immediate impact on business operations
  • Safe and inclusive workplace culture
If you are a safety-focused individual with strong administrative skills and an interest in transport and logistics, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and become part of a team committed to operational excellence and continuous improvement.

job.title: Sales Representative - Steel & Construction Materials
job.description:
Sales Representative - Steel & Construction Materials

Permanent Full-Time Opportunity | Perth, WA Join a Market-Leading Organisation Driving WA's Construction & Infrastructure Growth

Are you an experienced Sales Representative with a background in steel, construction materials, building products, or project-based sales?

An exciting opportunity exists for a motivated and commercially driven professional to join a well-established business supplying the construction, infrastructure, mining, residential, and commercial sectors across Western Australia.
This is more than a traditional sales role. We're looking for a proactive business development professional who thrives on building relationships, identifying opportunities, and securing major project work.

About the Role :
As a Sales Representative, you will be responsible for developing new business opportunities while managing and growing an established portfolio of customers. You'll engage with contractors, builders, developers, engineers, procurement teams, and key industry stakeholders to identify upcoming projects and provide tailored steel solutions.

This role combines technical sales, relationship management, and strategic business development, offering the opportunity to become a trusted industry advisor while contributing to the ongoing success of the business.

Key Responsibilities
  • Identify and secure new business opportunities across infrastructure, civil, mining, residential, and commercial construction sectors.
  • Develop and maintain a strong pipeline of project opportunities throughout Western Australia.
  • Actively pursue and convert new customer opportunities while growing existing accounts.
  • Monitor market activity, upcoming construction projects, and industry trends to identify opportunities for growth.
  • Develop strategic account plans and execute initiatives that drive sustainable revenue growth.
  • Provide technical advice and support on reinforcing steel, structural steel, and associated construction products.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with contractors, builders, engineers, developers, fabricators, and other key decision-makers.
  • Establish yourself as a trusted partner and industry resource for customers.
  • Strengthen existing client relationships while actively generating new opportunities.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service throughout the project lifecycle
  • Achieve sales, growth, and profitability targets.
  • Manage forecasting, pipeline reporting, and sales activity planning.
  • Provide accurate market intelligence and business development reporting.
  • Support account management activities, including ensuring strong commercial outcomes and timely account payments.

Essential Skills & Experience
  • Minimum 5 years' experience in steel sales, construction materials sales, building products, or a related industry.
  • Strong knowledge of reinforcing steel, structural steel, concrete products, or heavy construction materials.
  • Proven success in business development, account management, and project-based sales.
  • Experience working within the construction, infrastructure, mining, civil, engineering, or commercial sectors.
  • Strong negotiation, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain a sustainable project pipeline.
  • Experience managing forecasts, sales reporting, and customer relationships.
  • Current Australian Driver's Licence.
Highly Regarded
  • Ability to read and interpret structural drawings, project plans, and specifications.
  • Experience using CRM systems and sales management tools.
  • Established network of contacts within the WA construction, infrastructure, mining, or steel industries.
  • Understanding of project tendering processes and construction project lifecycles.
What's On Offer
  • Permanent full-time opportunity
  • Competitive salary package plus performance incentives
  • Company vehicle or vehicle allowance
  • Opportunity to work on major infrastructure, mining, and commercial construction projects
  • Career progression within a growing and respected industry
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment
  • Autonomy to build your territory and make a genuine impact on business growth
Apply Now If you're an experienced Sales Representative, Business Development Manager, Account Manager, or Steel Sales Professional looking to advance your career within the construction and infrastructure sector, we would love to hear from you.

Apply today with your resume and take the next step in your sales career.

  • Ability to interpret basic drawings and instructions
  • Physically fit and capable of manual handling duties
  • Reliable, motivated, and safety-focused
  • Forklift ticket highly regarded

  • Competitive hourly rate

job.title: Robotic Welder
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced MIG/GMAW Welders who are keen to step into the next phase of their career and learn robotic / 3D welding. This is a permanent full-time opportunity with a manufacturer producing high-strength metal components for the defence, maritime and aerospace industries.

If you enjoy quality-driven work, process control and modern manufacturing environments, this is a great role to build specialist skills on the job.

About the role
You’ll work with robotic GMAW welding cells—supporting start-up, running and shut-down, monitoring weld quality, and completing documentation to a high QA standard.
 
What you’ll need (essential)
  • Strong MIG/GMAW welding background
  • A positive attitude and genuine willingness to learn robotic welding
  • Ability to read engineering drawings / work packs and follow quality procedures
  • Comfortable using computers for production / QA documentation
  • Understanding of WPS and ability to adjust key variables (within procedure)
  • Strong focus on safety, quality and attention to detail
  • Experience in quality / process control OR leadership exposure (documentation-focused)
  • Australian citizenship
Qualification preferred: Certificate III in Mechanical Engineering (Fabrication stream) or equivalent trade background.
 
Desirable (nice to have)
  • Exposure to robot interfaces (offline programming experience highly regarded)
  • Fabrication experience related to robotic equipment / automation
  • AutoCAD experience
What’s on offer
  • Permanent full-time role
  • Mon–Fri Day & afternoon shift (infrequent overtime)
  • $90,000–$125,000 + super (depending on experience)
  • Structured training and development pathways
  • Modern facilities and advanced manufacturing processes
Apply now
Click Apply and submit your resume outlining your MIG/GMAW experience and any exposure to robotics, automation or quality documentation.

job.title: Warehouse Associate
job.description:
Warehouse Worker with Amazon

  • Work at Amazon Australia’s Delivery Station located in West Gosford.
  • Training and ongoing support provided
  • Flexible work with variable shift length - most shifts are min 4-5 hours per shift however flex will be needed as per business requirements.
  • Shifts generally will start from 4AM-5AM and this site operates 7 days a week therefore minimum 5 days availability a week will be needed.

Your starting rate of pay is $35.14. You get paid penalties if you work afternoon, early morning or weekend shifts!

About the role
This is a casual role where you will be required to be available across 5 days per week (including 1 day on the weekend). We have day and night shifts available with each shift being 4-10 hours long and weekly hours averaging between 15 - 38hrs per week. Experience is not required for these positions and full training is provided, however, an ability to follow instructions and standard processes is a must.

Responsibilities
  • Sorting & labeling of parcels and boxes being sent to and from the warehouse
  • Storing/stowing received parcels and boxes throughout the facility
  • Picking parcels and boxes from shelves using an RF scanner (training provided)
  • Organising and dispatching parcels and boxes that will be sent to the customer
  • Cleaning and organisation of the site environment
  • Adhering to safety, quality and production standards
  • Standing and walking for extended periods
  • Lifting and moving products up to 23kg in weight

Successful applicants will be employed by Chandler Macleod to carry out a temporary work assignment to Amazon and will be required to complete background and police check and a drug and alcohol test. You must also have the right to work in Australia.

About Amazon
Amazon is a company with 20+ years of operational expertise and technology advancements, where the future of retail and logistics is becoming reality. Your role is key in enabling everyday deliveries for customers and being on the front line of fulfilling Amazon’s customer promise. In return Amazon offers a safe, inclusive and fun environment to set you up for success so you can work hard, have fun and make history.
 

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Contact Centre Representative
job.description:
Contact Centre Representative
Location: Newcastle & hybrid once trained
Contract: Part time ongoing casual contract
Shifts: 4 half days per week (8am to 1pm OR 12pm to 5pm)
 
Broaden your customer service skills and gain top notch industry knowledge within a fast-paced yet supportive call-centre environment!

Chandler Macleod’s Business Support team are looking for dynamic contact centre representatives to join an iconic employer of choice in the Newcastle region.

Hunter Water is dedicated to delivering essential services including drinking water, wastewater, recycled water, and some stormwater management to more than 600,000 residents and businesses across the Lower Hunter region.  They strive to be a forward-thinking business that operates with vision and purpose. It's an exciting time to be part of their team.
  • Work for an organisation renowned for its excellent supportive team environment & brilliant work culture
  • Hybrid arrangements + modern harbourside offices
  • Opportunity to transition to permanent employment

About the role
As an experienced Contact Centre Representative, you are people-orientated and adaptable, with outstanding problem-solving skills. By applying knowledge, empathy and professionalism you will assess and fulfil customer needs as the first line of support through the Contact Centre.

Being a constant point of contact for customers, you can create and/or completely transform a customer’s experience. For this reason, it is important that you are approachable, friendly and well-informed with a passion for assisting people in times of need.

 To be successful in this role, you will:
  • Provide consistently high-quality customer service by interpreting and resolving first-contact enquiries across voice, digital, and email channels. This includes face to face interactions across the Customer Service centre.
  • Recognise and navigate the complexities in customer enquiries, identifying nuanced situations that may not fit into clear-cut categories.
  • Exceed customer expectations by proactively seeking opportunities to enhance their experience.
  • Identify and escalate more complex enquiries and transactions to ensure the timely and effective resolution of issues, providing regular updates to the customer.
  • Take an active interest in the Contact Centre and individual performance to achieve customer satisfaction and performance targets
  • Participate in regular quality assessments and in operational and performance discussions.
  • Actively engage in and support continuous improvement process within the Contact Centre
  • Effectively use a range of systems, technology and telephony solutions to undertake work tasks, triage, refer or escalate work tasks

About you
Demonstrating a desire to learn and progress within the role, you will actively seek and embrace feedback to identify areas for growth and improve overall performance.

Naturally, you’ll bring a commitment to customer service, business improvement, Company Values and Customer Commitment along with a strong team-focused work ethic with the ability to achieve individual and group objectives.

In addition you will have:
  • Minimum 1-2 years’ experience in a contact centre or customer service role across voice, digital, email, and face-to-face channels along with proven ability to deliver first-contact resolution and meet customer service targets
  • An ability to interpret complex data and confidently translate to customers in a professional manner
  • Confident to navigate multiple systems, technology platforms, and telephony tools to source relevant information quickly
  • Willingness to commit to reliable attendance of shifts and the requirement to work from the office on scheduled days
 
If this sounds like you, and you’re ready for your next new challenge, click the “Apply” button to submit your application or call Yolande on 02 4093 0966 for more details!

job.description:

Chandler Macleod is currently seeking a trade-qualified Auto Electrician to join a leading supplier of solar-powered lighting, communications, and surveillance equipment based in Kewdale, WA.

This workshop-based role is ideal for a mechanically minded Auto Electrician who enjoys a varied workload, combining electrical installation, fault finding, assembly, and mechanical fit-out work on innovative renewable energy equipment.

  • Solar lighting towers
  • Mobile communications units
  • CCTV and surveillance towers
  • Battery storage systems

This role is approximately 50/50 electrical and mechanical, making it ideal for someone who enjoys getting involved in all aspects of equipment build and maintenance. While electrical terminations, wiring, diagnostics, and commissioning are key components of the role, you must also be willing to undertake mechanical assembly, fit-out, modifications, and general workshop duties.

job.title: Manager, Research Contracts
job.description:
Manager, Research Contracts | $94.11 p/h + Super | Melbourne CBD
Hybrid Working | University Environment | Immediate Start | Potential Extension

We are currently seeking an experienced Manager, Research Contracts to join a leading university based in Melbourne CBD.

This is an excellent opportunity for a commercially minded professional with strong contract law knowledge, negotiation skills and the ability to navigate complex contractual arrangements.

We welcome applications from experienced contracts professionals, legal practitioners and internationally qualified lawyers currently residing in Melbourne who are looking to utilise their legal expertise within the Australian workforce.

The OpportunityReporting to the Senior Manager, Research Contracts, you will be responsible for reviewing, drafting and negotiating a broad range of commercial and research-related agreements.

These agreements may include research funding arrangements, collaborative research partnerships, intellectual property licensing and commercial research contracts.

Working closely with internal legal, finance and risk teams, as well as external funding bodies and industry partners, you will provide commercially sound advice, manage contractual risks and facilitate successful outcomes.

This position offers a high degree of autonomy within a collaborative university environment.


Key Responsibilities
  • Review, draft and negotiate commercial contracts, research agreements, funding arrangements and collaborative partnerships.
  • Assess contractual risks relating to intellectual property, insurance, indemnities and compliance obligations.
  • Provide practical commercial and contractual advice to internal stakeholders.
  • Negotiate contractual terms with external funding agencies, research collaborators and industry partners.
  • Collaborate with legal, finance and risk teams to ensure agreements comply with organisational policies.
  • Identify potential contractual risks and recommend commercially viable solutions.
  • Prepare recommendations to support informed decisions regarding contract execution.
  • Maintain accurate contractual documentation, records and reporting.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement across contract management processes.

About You
We are seeking a professional with strong legal knowledge, commercial awareness and the confidence to interpret and negotiate complex agreements.
Ideally, you will demonstrate:

Working within the Australian Submarine Agency environment, the Requirements Management and Analysis Technical Specialist (APS6) is accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for providing technical expertise, systems administration support, analysis and stakeholder engagement to enable effective requirements management and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) practices.

The directorate enables informed and evidence-based decision-making by supporting the development, management, governance and assurance of capability requirements throughout the capability lifecycle.
The directorate’s functions align with the principles of a nuclear mindset through a commitment to technical excellence, procedural compliance, accountability, traceability, a questioning attitude and continuous learning.

Key Responsibilities

You will be responsible for supporting and delivering requirements management and MBSE outcomes, including:
  • Providing technical expertise and system administration support for the RMS and associated engineering tools

job.title: Study Manager
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is partnering with a well-established, large-scale organisation in the resources / heavy industry space to recruit an experienced Study Manager to lead a major greenfield Concept Study (FEL1). This is a key appointment as the project pipeline grows, offering the chance to influence early investment decisions and shape the definition of a significant future program of work.

This role will suit someone who is confident operating in ambiguity, comfortable facilitating alignment (without losing objectivity), and experienced producing decision-quality study outcomes for senior stakeholders.

The Opportunity

As Study Manager, you will establish and lead the early-phase study approach—bringing disciplined study and project management practices to test strategic fit, technical viability, value, risk, and execution pathways before material capital is committed. You’ll work across a complex, evolving environment with multiple internal and external interfaces, coordinating multidisciplinary inputs and ensuring study recommendations are supported by clear evidence, transparent assumptions, and fit-for-purpose governance.

Key responsibilities

Health, safety and environment
  • Provide visible leadership and ensure study delivery aligns with HSE requirements, policies and critical risk controls.
Study planning & delivery (FEL1 and potentially FEL2–3)
  • Define the study strategy, scope, objectives, deliverables, basis of study and execution plan
  • Lead an integrated team to deliver study outputs safely, on time and within budget
  • Build and maintain realistic schedules, resource plans, budgets and forecasts (including forward estimates for subsequent phases)
Business case development
  • Develop commercially relevant, decision-ready business cases assessing:
    • options and trade-offs
    • costs, schedule, value drivers and key assumptions
    • risks, opportunities and sustainability impacts
    • execution and implementation pathways
Options / trade-off analysis
  • Structure and facilitate workshops and working sessions for:
    • opportunity framing
    • optioneering / range analysis
    • trade-off decision making
  • Ensure options are evaluated consistently and recommendations are traceable to agreed criteria.
Risk, assurance and governance
  • Maintain risk, opportunity, assumptions and decision registers
  • Coordinate peer reviews / technical reviews / independent assurance and close out actions
  • Provide concise reporting on progress, cost, schedule, risk, decisions and required interventions
Stakeholder management
  • Engage across operational, technical, commercial and corporate stakeholder groups
  • Build strong working relationships with senior leaders and external parties
  • Lead decision forums and stakeholder workshops to create alignment while preserving constructive challenge
External service providers
  • Develop scopes of work, support procurement, and manage consultants/service providers to meet safety, quality, cost and schedule expectations.
About you (selection criteria)

To be successful in this role, you will bring a strong blend of study leadership, stakeholder influence, and delivery discipline.

Essential
  • Demonstrated experience delivering early-phase Concept and/or Pre-Feasibility studies in mining, minerals processing, heavy industry, manufacturing or comparable sectors
  • Strong study/project management capability with an ability to lead multidisciplinary inputs
  • Proven experience managing complex stakeholder groups, including senior executives and external parties
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills (reports, executive papers, presentations, workshops)
  • Relevant tertiary qualification (engineering, metallurgy, chemistry, project management, business or related) or extensive equivalent industry experience
  • Willingness and ability to travel to site as required
Highly regarded
  • 15+ years’ experience across resources / heavy industry development, studies or major projects
  • Exposure to complex processing operations (e.g., refineries, concentrators, smelters or similar)
  • Formal project/study management training and/or recognised certification
  • Experience facilitating structured processes such as range analysis, opportunity framing and optioneering
  • Risk management / process safety / technical assurance experience

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced and commercially astute Regional Manager to take full ownership of a leading heavy vehicle and transport solutions operation, driving sales growth, workshop performance, parts operations, customer relationships, and overall branch profitability.

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on leader who understands the heavy vehicle industry from the ground up. Two opportunities are available, located in Sydney and Brisbane.

Who We're Looking For

We're seeking a genuine industry leader who has progressed from a hands-on workshop or production environment into senior management. You understand the operational realities of a heavy vehicle, manufacturing, or service-based business and combine this experience with strong commercial acumen, customer relationship management skills, and a proven ability to lead high-performing teams while driving sustainable business growth and profitability.

About the Role

Reporting to senior leadership, you will have full responsibility for the strategic and operational performance of your state operation.

With complete P&L accountability, you will oversee:

• New and used equipment sales
• Workshop service, repairs and maintenance operations
• Spare parts sales and inventory management
• Customer service and after-sales support
• Safety, compliance and facility management
• Team leadership, coaching and performance

This role requires a balance of commercial acumen and operational leadership, with the ability to move seamlessly between customer meetings, sales strategy, workshop operations, and financial management.

What You'll Bring

Essential Experience
5+ years' experience leading a branch, region or business unit within:
• Heavy vehicles
• Transport equipment
• Manufacturing
• Automotive OEM
• Truck or equipment servicing operations
• Strong commercial and financial management capability
• Proven leadership experience with direct P&L responsibility
• Demonstrated success managing customer relationships and driving revenue growth
• Experience leading workshop and operational teams
Highly Desirable
• Trade qualification in Diesel Mechanics, Fabrication, Welding or a related discipline
• Experience within the heavy vehicle, transport equipment or manufacturing sectors
• Understanding of heavy vehicle repairs, maintenance and aftermarket parts operations
• Existing network across transport, logistics or fleet customers

Success in This Role Looks Like

• Achieving branch EBIT and profitability targets
• Growing equipment sales and market share
• Improving workshop productivity and turnaround times
• Expanding parts revenue and inventory performance
• Delivering exceptional customer outcomes
• Building an engaged, accountable and high-performing team

Why Join?

• Lead a significant state operation within a well-established industry leader
• Genuine autonomy with full state responsibility
• Executive-level influence and visibility
• Strong support from a national leadership team
• Opportunity to drive growth and shape the future of the business
• Competitive salary package including vehicle and incentive structure

Apply Now

If you've come from the workshop floor, understand the transport industry, and have developed into a commercially driven business leader, we'd love to hear from you.

Submit your resume and cover letter via the Apply Now link.

We currently have two opportunities available, based in Sydney and Brisbane.

For a copy of the Position Description or a confidential discussion about either role, please contact Jo Ellerman on (02) 6691 9106.

job.description:
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Senior Development Engineer to assess and manage engineering aspects of development applications, subdivision works and major development projects. This role plays a key part in ensuring development outcomes meet engineering, environmental and community standards while protecting Council infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities
  • Assess engineering components of Development Applications (DAs), Subdivision Works Certificates and Subdivision Certificates.
  • Supervise civil construction works associated with subdivisions and major developments.
  • Provide expert advice on stormwater, on-site detention, drainage, roads, erosion and sediment control, traffic matters and vehicle access.
  • Review engineering designs and ensure compliance with Council standards and industry best practice.
  • Prepare assessment reports, engineering conditions and recommendations within required timeframes.
  • Liaise with developers, consultants, contractors, government agencies and internal stakeholders.
  • Mentor Development Engineers and provide specialist technical advice on complex projects.
About You
You will be a highly experienced Civil Engineer with a strong background in land development, subdivision projects and development assessment.

Essential Requirements
  • Degree in Civil Engineering.
  • Current NSW Class C Driver Licence.
  • Extensive experience in development engineering, civil design and construction associated with urban development.
  • Strong knowledge of roads, drainage, stormwater, flooding, traffic and water quality management principles.
  • Experience assessing Development Applications, Subdivision Works Certificates and Subdivision Certificates.
  • Knowledge of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 and related legislation.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
Highly Regarded
  • Local Government development engineering experience.
  • Land subdivision expertise.
  • Postgraduate qualifications in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Working knowledge of the Local Government Act and Roads Act.

job.title: Track Protection Officer
job.description:
Track Protection Officer (TPO)

• Competitive hourly pay range + super paid on all hours worked
• 2/2 roster | FIFO from Perth
• Opportunity working at Rio Tinto at Dampier

About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Track Protection Officer (TPO) to support ballast cleaning operations across the Rio Tinto Rail Network.

This is a great opportunity to join a safety-focused team working on site with Rio Tinto. You'll work alongside experienced crews, supporting day-to-day operations while contributing to safe and reliable outcomes.

Reporting to the Rail Supervisor / Superintendent, your responsibilities will include:

• Prepare, verify and implement Track Protection Plans and work-on-track authority requirements
• Confirm worksite limits, access points, safe places, adjacent line risks and protection requirements prior to starting
• Establish, maintain and remove field protection controls in accordance with approved safeworking requirements
• Conduct pre-start and safeworking briefings, including sign-on processes, hazards and emergency arrangements
• Coordinate with Train Control, supervisors, PPOs, maintainers, contractors and ballast cleaning crews to ensure safe work execution
• Monitor and respond to changing site conditions including rail traffic exposure, machine movements, fatigue, weather and scope changes
• Exercise the authority to stop work and escalate concerns immediately where protection, communication, authority or behaviours are unsafe/non-compliant
• Complete all required documentation, handovers, authority cancellations and close-out records within required timeframes

About You

• Demonstrated experience as a Track Protection Officer / Protection Officer / Safeworking professionalwithin rail maintenance or possession environments
• Experience working in heavy haul railand/or major maintenance campaigns (ballast cleaning, tamping, rail grinding, renewals or track machine operations highly regarded)
• Current Track Protection Officer competency (network relevant) and strong knowledge of safeworking systems, permits and protection authorities
• Happy to work a varied roster (12/9 and 2/2) with a mix of days and nights
• Valid Australian C-Class Driver’s Licence
• Strong teamwork and communication skills
• Dedication to everyone’s safety, including confidence to challenge unsafe work and stop the job when required
• Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing, and meet Rio Tinto onboarding, site access and VOC requirements

Why Join Chandler Macleod?

• Competitive hourly pay range paid weekly
• Superannuation paid on all hours worked
• Consistent roster and work-life balance
• Opportunity to gain experience with Rio Tinto
• Dedicated Chandler Macleod support team
• Access to future opportunities across Rio Tinto operations

Apply Now!
Ready to take the next step in your career? Join Chandler Macleod and work with Rio Tinto at one of Australia's leading mining operations. We're recruiting now and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

FIFO from Perth | 2:1 Roster | 12-Month Opportunity | ASAP Start

A major iron ore operation in Western Australia is seeking an experienced Electrical Commissioning Supervisor to lead the safe and successful commissioning and energisation of electrical systems across a large-scale mining project.
This is a hands-on leadership role where you will work closely with engineering, construction, operations, and HSE teams to ensure all electrical systems are tested, verified, commissioned, and handed over in accordance with project specifications, Australian standards, and site safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
Project Coordination
  • Plan and manage commissioning activities in line with construction schedules and project milestones.
  • Coordinate closely with engineering, construction, and HSE teams to ensure commissioning readiness.
  • Review electrical drawings, specifications, and commissioning procedures for accuracy and completeness.
Leadership & Supervision
  • Lead, mentor, and supervise commissioning technicians, electricians, and subcontractors.
  • Allocate work, monitor progress, and maintain high standards of quality and safety.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Provide technical guidance and resolve commissioning-related issues.
Testing & Commissioning
  • Oversee installation verification, pre-commissioning, and functional testing of:
    • HV/LV electrical systems
    • Switchgear
    • Transformers
    • Motor Control Centres (MCCs)
    • Control panels and associated infrastructure
  • Witness and validate test results to ensure compliance with project and regulatory requirements.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve electrical faults during commissioning and start-up activities.
Safety & Compliance
  • Ensure all commissioning activities comply with site HSE requirements, electrical safety standards, and permit-to-work systems.
  • Lead toolbox talks and promote safe work practices across the team.
  • Maintain accurate records of audits, incidents, and corrective actions.
Documentation & Reporting
  • Prepare commissioning reports, test certificates, and handover documentation.
  • Maintain accurate records of commissioning progress and system status.
  • Escalate risks, technical issues, and project delays to project leadership.
Quality Assurance
  • Verify installations meet design intent and relevant Australian Standards.
  • Identify and rectify defects before project handover.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and lessons learned reviews.
About You
Essential
  • Electrical Trade Certificate or Degree in Electrical Engineering.
  • Current WA Electrical Licence.
  • Minimum 10 years' experience in electrical commissioning within mining, resources, or heavy industrial environments.
  • Prior experience working in FIFO and remote site operations.

Skills & Attributes
  • Strong knowledge of electrical systems, protection schemes, and commissioning processes.

  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities.

job.title: Sales & Customer Service Representative
job.description:
We are seeking a commercially minded and personable Sales & Customer Service Representative to join an established plant and equipment hire business based in Dandenong South.

This is a hands-on, phone-based role focused on maintaining strong client relationships and generating dry hire opportunities across the civil and construction industries.

A large part of your day will involve proactively contacting existing and previous clients, keeping the business front of mind and understanding their upcoming projects and equipment requirements. You'll also manage inbound hire enquiries, prepare and follow up quotes, re-engage dormant clients and identify opportunities to develop new business.

There is a genuine sales element to the role, so you'll need to be comfortable picking up the phone, starting conversations and asking for the business. However, this isn't a traditional BDM position focused solely on cold acquisition or being out on the road.

Working within a small, close-knit team, you'll also be someone who is happy to jump in and assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries when needed.


Key Responsibilities
  • Proactively contact existing, previous and prospective clients to generate hire opportunities
  • Build and maintain relationships with clients across the civil and construction sectors
  • Re-engage dormant clients and identify upcoming projects or equipment requirements
  • Manage inbound hire enquiries via phone and email
  • Prepare quotes and proactively follow up outstanding opportunities
  • Identify and approach prospective clients where appropriate
  • Promote available equipment to maximise fleet utilisation
  • Maintain accurate client and sales activity within HubSpot CRM
  • Assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries across the office when required
  • Conduct phone and Microsoft Teams meetings, with occasional site visits where beneficial
  • Work closely with the wider team to maintain client engagement and sales momentum

About You
We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys speaking with clients and is comfortable with the commercial side of relationship building.

You'll ideally be:
  • Confident making proactive outbound calls and asking clients about upcoming requirements
  • Personable, genuine and able to build rapport quickly
  • Commercially minded and comfortable identifying sales opportunities
  • Comfortable approaching new clients as well as working with established relationships
  • Persistent with follow-ups without being overly pushy
  • Reliable, consistent and willing to get involved wherever needed
  • Organised and disciplined with quotes, follow-ups and CRM activity
  • Comfortable working autonomously within a small office environment
  • Looking for a stable, long-term opportunity where you can become a valued part of the team

Experience within plant and equipment hire, earthmoving, civil construction, construction or a related industry will be highly regarded. Strong internal sales, hire or client relationship experience from another industry will also be considered.


What's on Offer
  • $80,000–$85,000 + super
  • Permanent, full-time opportunity
  • Dandenong South location
  • 100% office-based, with occasional site visits
  • Small, close-knit and down-to-earth team
  • Established client relationships to build upon
  • A varied mix of client relationships, hire coordination and proactive sales
  • Stable, long-term opportunity within an established business

job.title: Leasing Executive
job.description:
The Company

Our client, a global leader in it's field is looking to recruit a Leasing Executive to join the team based in Brisbane's southern suburbs.

The Role

In this newly created role, you will take a proactive role in managing the commercial leasing requirements of the national tenant portfolio.
Your primary focus will be identifying opportunities to reduce occupancy costs, negotiate favourable lease terms, secure rental incentives and improve flexibility across the existing tenancy commitments.
You will also manage new leasing transactions, relocations and consolidations, ensuring property decisions are supported by market intelligence, financial analysis and operational requirements.


Key Responsibilities


Lease Negotiations & Cost Optimisation

  • Proactively manage lease renewals, expiries, options and critical dates.
  • Lead negotiations with landlords and agents to secure competitive rental terms, incentives, rent abatements and favourable lease conditions.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce occupancy costs through rental renegotiations, lease restructuring and improved commercial arrangements.
  • Negotiate lease flexibility, including break clauses, make-good provisions, rent reviews and other key commercial terms.
  • Tenant Portfolio Monitor and report on negotiated savings, lease incentives and cost-reduction initiatives.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to ensure leasing arrangements align with operational and contractual requirements.


Strategic Leasing & Site Selection

  • Manage targeted property searches and new leasing requirements.
  • Assess suitable premises against business needs, location requirements and financial objectives.
  • Negotiate heads of agreement and commercial terms for new tenancies.
  • Coordinate leasing transactions through to execution in collaboration with legal, finance and operational teams.

Landlord & Stakeholder Relationships

  • Build and maintain effective relationships with landlords, managing agents and commercial property representatives.
  • Provide commercial leasing advice and recommendations to internal stakeholders.
  • Work collaboratively across the business to deliver commercially sound leasing outcomes.


About You

You are a confident negotiator with strong commercial instincts, analytical capability and a proactive approach to managing tenant leasing requirements.

You have:

  • Extensive experience in commercial leasing
  • Demonstrated success negotiating lease renewals, rental reductions, incentives and favourable commercial terms.
  • Strong understanding of commercial lease structures, occupancy costs and Australian leasing practices.
  • Ability to analyse rental markets, assess financial opportunities and develop commercial recommendations.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication and negotiation skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly around lease obligations, critical dates and commercial risks.
  • Ability to work independently and as a part of a team, prioritise competing requirements and deliver measurable outcomes.


What's on Offer

  • An opportunity to influence leasing outcomes across an established national tenant portfolio.
  • A commercially focused role with autonomy and accountability.
  • Exposure to complex negotiations, strategic leasing initiatives and cost optimisation projects.
  • A collaborative working environment with engagement across senior management.
  • Hybrid working environment
  • Competitive remuneration package

If interested, then please apply now. This role is to be filled as soon as possible and interviews will be conducted this week and early next.

job.title: Material and Logistics Officer
job.description:
About the Company Join a leading organisation dedicated to decarbonisation projects within the energy and resources sector. Focused on sustainable initiatives, this company is at the forefront of reducing environmental impact and driving innovative solutions to power a cleaner future. Based in Perth, it’s a dynamic place to grow your career while contributing to meaningful change.

Ready to be part of something meaningful? Apply now and bring your expertise to a workplace where your contributions truly matter!

job.title: Contracts Supervisor
job.description:

job.title: Digital Testing Lead
job.description:
Digital Testing Lead
  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto
  • 5-month assignment via Chandler Macleod
  • Safety-first culture with supportive teams
About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Digital Testing Lead to join the Finance Digital team.

Entering the project during mid-build, the Digital Testing Lead will lead user acceptance testing for Finance Digital products and changes, making sure business users can test effectively and that the project has a clear, evidence-based view of readiness for release.

Key Responsibilities
  • Plan and coordinate UAT activities with business representatives, product owners and the delivery team.
  • Define test scenarios, test cases and acceptance criteria with the relevant business users.
  • Prepare testers, coordinate testing sessions and keep the test schedule on track.
  • Record, prioritise and follow up defects, issues and decisions arising through UAT.
  • Work with delivery and technical teams to ensure defects are understood, resolved and retested.
  • Provide clear reporting on test progress, outstanding risks and readiness for release.
  • Maintain UAT evidence, including test outcomes, defect status and business sign-off.
  • Identify gaps in test coverage or business readiness early and escalate them appropriately.

To be successful in this role, you encompass;
  • Experience leading or coordinating UAT in a business, finance, systems or digital-delivery environment.
  • Able to work comfortably with business users who have varying levels of technical confidence.
  • Strong organisation and follow-through across multiple testers, scenarios and competing priorities.
  • Clear written communication, particularly for defects, risks, test outcomes and release-readiness reporting.
  • Can demonstrate practical judgement about what needs escalation and what can be resolved within the delivery team.
  • Experience with the SAP Analytic Cloud (SAC) and SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) will be highly regarded but not critical.

Apply now!
 If you are organised, calm under pressure and prepared to seek clarification when testing outcomes are unclear, we would love to hear from you.

  • Provide regular reporting on workforce performance, attendance and key metrics

To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:

  • Previous exposure to construction, mining, infrastructure or renewable energy projects is preferred but not essential
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills
  • Excellent organisational and problem solving abilities
  • The ability to work independently while managing competing priorities
  • A sound understanding of workplace health and safety requirements
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills
  • A current Australian Driver's Licence

What's On Offer
  • Competitive salary package plus allowances
  • Ongoing training and professional development
  • Career progression opportunities within a national organisation
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment
  • Opportunity to work on a landmark project

job.title: Inventory Controller
job.description:
Stores & Inventory Controller
Matraville, NSW
Ongoing Casual Role
38 Hours Per Week | Monday to Friday | Onsite Parking Available

An established industrial manufacturing operation is seeking a hands-on Stores & Inventory Controller to support site stores, inventory accuracy, equipment refurbishment processes, and chemical reporting activities.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys combining physical warehouse responsibilities with inventory administration and reporting. You will play a key role in ensuring critical engineering spares, consumables, and chemicals are accurately managed to support site operations.

Key Responsibilities
  • Support equipment refurbishment processes through SAP while ensuring accurate records and transactions
  • Receive, inspect, and issue engineering spares, consumables, and chemicals
  • Process goods movements against SAP purchase orders and work orders
  • Verify deliveries including quantities, part numbers and condition
  • Report damaged, incorrect or non-conforming inventory items
  • Pick and prepare materials for maintenance, shutdown and production activities
  • Complete weekly and monthly chemical reporting
  • Liaise with suppliers and internal finance teams regarding inventory and reporting requirements
  • Investigate stock discrepancies, transaction errors and master data issues
  • Maintain compliance standards relating to hazardous materials and stores operations
  • Identify opportunities to improve inventory accuracy, stock availability and process efficiency
To be successful, you will have:
  • Current Forklift Licence (highly regarded, but not mandatory)
  • Demonstrated SAP experience
  • Previous stores, warehouse, inventory or spare parts coordination experience
  • Strong administrative and reporting skills
  • Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills
  • Excellent attention to detail and data accuracy
  • Ability to prioritise competing demands in a busy environment
  • Strong commitment to workplace safety
  • Proactive and self-motivated approach to work
Benefits
  • Long-term temporary opportunity
  • Stable Monday to Friday roster
  • Onsite parking provided
  • Varied role combining stores operations and administration
  • Opportunity to contribute to inventory and process improvement initiatives
To apply, click Apply Now or email ashish.bhetwal@chandlermacleod.com

job.title: SMP/Mechanical Project Supervisors
job.description:
The Opportunity
Chandler Macleod is partnering with a major iron ore producer to recruit two experienced SMP/Mechanical Project Supervisors to support a major brownfield project in the Eastern Pilbar.

You’ll play a key role supervising site execution for the replacement of the Train Loadout Facility and supporting infrastructure, ensuring safe delivery, schedule adherence, and quality outcomes across SMP/mechanical scopes.

Key Responsibilities
  • Supervise mechanical/SMP activities across project and shutdown environments
  • Lead crews and contractors to deliver works safely, efficiently and to standard
  • Coordinate daily execution plans, permits, isolation/LOTO and work packs
  • Monitor progress against schedule; resolve constraints and escalate risks early

What You’ll Need

  • Shutdown / major project execution experience in mining or heavy industry
  • S26 (DMIRS) qualification – mandatory
  • Strong safety leadership, contractor management capability, and clear communication
  • Ability to work on-site on an 8:6 roster in the Central Pilbara
Why This Role
  • Immediate project demand with new projects starting now
  • Competitive contract rate ($105/hr + super PAYG
  • 12-month initial contract with genuine extension opportunities on ongoing works
  • Work with a tier-one operator on a high-profile site infrastructure upgrade

Apply Now

If you’re an SMP/Mechanical Supervisor with a strong mechanical background and S26, we’d like to hear from you. Please apply with your CV and a brief summary of your availability (ideally aligned to 28/10/2026 or 04/11/2026 start).

job.title: Audit and Assurance Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Audit & Assurance Officer to support governance, risk, audit and business continuity functions within a Federal Government environment. This is an excellent opportunity for a governance professional with strong audit, assurance and stakeholder engagement experience to contribute to organisational resilience and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Locations: Albury NSW, Griffith NSW,  Canberra ACT, Goondiwindi QLD, Mildura VIC, Adelaide SA , Murray Bridge SA,
  • Contract: 12-month contract with potential extension
  • Work Arrangement: Flexible working arrangements may be considered

About the Role
As the APS 6 Audit & Assurance Officer, you will play a key role in coordinating internal audit programs, supporting assurance and risk management activities, maintaining governance frameworks, and contributing to business continuity planning. You will work closely with senior stakeholders, governance committees, external providers and business areas to strengthen organisational performance and compliance.

Key Responsibilities
  • Coordinate and manage the delivery of internal audits, including planning, stakeholder engagement, audit monitoring and reporting.
  • Maintain audit recommendation registers, track management actions and provide timely reporting to leadership and governance committees.
  • Manage relationships with internal audit service providers and support assurance, compliance and risk management activities.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, briefings and committee papers relating to audit, risk, assurance and business continuity.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of governance, risk and assurance frameworks, policies and processes.
  • Support business continuity planning, testing activities and organisational resilience initiatives.
  • Coordinate external reviews, risk workshops and assurance activities as required.

About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Experience in audit, assurance, risk management, governance or compliance within a complex organisation.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify trends, risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing reports, briefings and executive-level documentation.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes within tight timeframes.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Experience supporting governance committees and working with senior leaders.
  • Knowledge of business continuity frameworks and organisational resilience practices will be highly regarded.
  • Experience within a Federal Government environment is desirable.


At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

job.title: HR Specialists & Talent Advisors - Multiple 6 month opportunities
job.description:
Multiple 6-Month Temporary Opportunities | Level 4 & Level 6 | Public Sector

Are you an experienced HR professional looking to contribute to high-profile workforce projects within a public sector environment?
We are seeking talented HR practitioners to join a specialist People & Culture team for six-month temporary assignments. These opportunities will suit professionals with experience in job evaluation and classification, senior executive employment arrangements, or talent acquisition and recruitment.
With multiple vacancies available across several HR disciplines, this is an excellent opportunity to apply your expertise in a collaborative and fast-paced environment.

Available Opportunities

HR Specialist - Classification & Job Evaluation (Level 6)

We are seeking an experienced HR professional with demonstrated expertise in position classification and work value assessment, ideally within the WA public sector or a comparable government environment.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Reviewing and assessing Job Description Forms (JDFs)
  • Conducting job classification and work value assessments
  • Providing clear, evidence-based classification advice
  • Preparing supporting documentation and recommendations
  • Contributing to organisational workforce and position management initiatives
Experience applying the BIPERS job evaluation methodology will be highly regarded.

HR Specialist - Senior Executive Service Support (Level 6)

This role will support senior executive employment and classification activities within a government setting.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Undertaking Senior Executive Service (SES) classification assessments
  • Preparing classification and appointment business cases
  • Coordinating submissions to relevant government authorities
  • Supporting SES recruitment and appointment processes
  • Providing advice on executive employment arrangements and frameworks
Applicants with previous experience supporting SES or equivalent executive employment arrangements are encouraged to apply.

Talent Advisors (2 Positions Available) - Level 4

We are seeking proactive recruitment professionals to support end-to-end talent acquisition activities.
Working closely with hiring managers and stakeholders, you will play a key role in attracting, sourcing and securing high-quality talent across a diverse range of positions.
Responsibilities may include:
  • Managing recruitment and selection processes
  • Providing advice on recruitment policies and procedures
  • Drafting and advertising vacancies
  • Coordinating assessments, interviews and appointment processes
  • Building strong relationships with hiring managers and candidates
  • Supporting workforce planning and talent attraction initiatives
About You

To be successful, you will demonstrate:
  • Relevant HR, recruitment, workforce or organisational development experience
  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality outcomes
  • Sound analytical, report writing and problem-solving capabilities
  • Experience within the WA public sector or government environment will be highly regarded
What's on Offer?
  • Multiple six-month temporary opportunities
  • Attractive public sector remuneration
  • Opportunity to contribute to significant workforce projects
  • Collaborative and supportive team environment
  • Valuable experience within a large and complex organisation
Whether your expertise lies in classification and job evaluation, senior executive employment, or talent acquisition, we welcome applications from experienced HR professionals looking to make an immediate impact.

job.title: Senior Manager Communication and Engagement
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Senior Manager Communication & Engagement to lead strategic community engagement and stakeholder communication activities across a nationally significant infrastructure program.

This senior leadership opportunity will see you driving engagement strategies, managing complex stakeholder relationships, leading a high-performing team, and ensuring community feedback is effectively integrated into project planning and delivery. The role plays a critical part in building trust, maintaining social licence, and supporting the successful delivery of major infrastructure outcomes. 
  • Contract: 12-month contract with potential extension
  • Locations: Location: Sydney, Canberra, Newcastle OR Central Coast
  • Work Arrangement: 
    • On-site role with flexible work arrangements to balance operational and team needs.
    • Regular travel across project locations and other HSRA offices. Some evening and weekend work will be required to support engagement activities and operational commitments.

About the Role
Reporting to the General Manager, Project Communication, you will provide strategic leadership across communication and engagement activities within a designated project region. You will oversee engagement programs, manage sensitive stakeholder matters, and guide teams through complex community, property and construction-related issues.
This role requires a highly experienced communications professional who can operate confidently in politically sensitive environments while delivering outstanding stakeholder outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership
  • Lead the development and execution of communication and community engagement strategies aligned to organisational objectives.
  • Provide expert advice on complex stakeholder, community and project-related matters.
  • Manage and mentor an experienced team of engagement professionals.
  • Drive continuous improvement, governance and compliance across engagement activities.
  • Contribute to strategic planning and organisational priorities.

Stakeholder Engagement & Communications
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with community members, landowners, government agencies and key stakeholders.
  • Manage sensitive and potentially contentious issues with professionalism and sound judgement.
  • Act as a senior representative in stakeholder meetings, community forums and public engagements.
  • Support issue resolution, complaints management and risk mitigation activities.
  • Develop innovative communication initiatives that foster transparency and trust.

Project Delivery & Reporting
  • Monitor stakeholder sentiment, emerging risks and community concerns.
  • Prepare executive-level reports, briefings and strategic insights.
  • Oversee engagement data collection, analysis and reporting.
  • Ensure engagement activities comply with legislative, regulatory and policy requirements.
  • Support procurement and administrative activities as required.

About You
To be successful, you will bring:
  • Extensive experience (10+ years) in community engagement, stakeholder relations, public affairs or communications leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated success delivering engagement strategies for major infrastructure, government or large-scale projects.
  • Experience managing complex stakeholder environments, including planning approvals, property acquisition, construction impacts and community issues.
  • Proven ability to lead high-performing teams and foster collaborative workplace cultures.
  • Strong strategic communications, negotiation and conflict resolution skills.
  • Experience preparing executive briefings, reports and strategic recommendations.
  • Strong project management capabilities with the ability to manage risks, priorities and competing stakeholder interests.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Project Manager (Specialist Projects)
job.description:
Project Manager (Specialist Projects)
Kurri Kurri, NSW
Attractive Salary Package

Our client is seeking an experienced and results-driven Project Manager to join their Project Delivery team based in Kurri Kurri, NSW.

This is an exciting opportunity to lead a diverse portfolio of sustaining and capital projects across mobile delivery systems, infrastructure upgrades, commissioning activities, asset mobilisation, and operational improvement initiatives.

About the Role Reporting to the Lead Projects, you will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of multiple projects, ensuring outcomes are achieved safely, on time, within budget, and to the highest standards.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Managing multiple sustaining and capital projects simultaneously.
  • Developing project scopes, schedules, budgets, and risk management plans.
  • Coordinating contractors, suppliers, procurement activities, and project resources.
  • Managing project governance, reporting, forecasting, and project controls.
  • Leading mobilisation, construction, commissioning, and handover activities.
  • Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Driving projects through to successful completion while balancing competing priorities.
About You
We are looking for a practical project professional with a strong delivery focus and the ability to navigate complexity.

You may come from a background in:
  • Project Delivery
  • Mining
  • Fixed Plant or Mobile Equipment
  • Civil Construction
  • Heavy Manufacturing
  • Maintenance and Shutdowns
  • Operations or Logistics
  • Trades or Construction Supervision
While engineering qualifications may be beneficial, this is not a design engineering role. We are particularly interested in candidates who have successfully coordinated and delivered projects within operational, maintenance, construction, or manufacturing environments. Formal project management qualifications will be highly regarded.

What Will Make You Successful

The ideal candidate will:
  • Make sound decisions with incomplete information.
  • Thrive in ambiguous and changing environments.
  • Balance competing stakeholder expectations.
  • Drive outcomes despite uncertainty.
  • Maintain strong ownership and accountability.
  • Be highly organised and capable of managing multiple projects concurrently.
  • Hold stakeholders accountable and follow through on commitments.
  • Focus on delivering practical outcomes rather than pursuing technical perfection.
In short, we're looking for someone who can bring structure to complexity, coordinate multiple stakeholders, and consistently deliver successful project outcomes.

Key Requirements
  • 5+ years' experience managing capital and/or sustaining projects.
  • Qualifications in Project Management, Engineering, Construction, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Strong contractor management and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Demonstrated experience managing project budgets, schedules, and risk.
  • Excellent communication, planning, and organisational skills.
  • Experience working within industrial, manufacturing, mining, maintenance, or construction environments.
What's on Offer
  • Attractive salary package.
  • Opportunity to manage a diverse portfolio of projects with significant business impact.
  • Supportive and collaborative project delivery environment.
  • Minimal travel requirements (less than 10%).
  • Based in Kurri Kurri, NSW.
If you're a proactive Project Manager who enjoys creating order from complexity, influencing stakeholders, and delivering outcomes, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Safety Advisor
job.description:
Safety Advisor | Construction

$966 per day inclusive of super | Truganina
Initial 12-month contract | Long-term opportunity through to April 2028
Full-time | 3 days per week onsite

We are seeking an experienced Safety Advisor to provide dedicated health and safety assurance across a large-scale construction and operational environment in Truganina.

This role will work across a complex multi-contractor site, providing safety advice, assurance and oversight during construction activities that interface with operational teams. You’ll partner closely with internal safety and project stakeholders, the Principal Contractor, subcontractors and site leadership to support safe work practices and strong safety outcomes.

Importantly, this is an assurance and advisory role. It does not replace or assume the safety management responsibilities of the Principal Contractor or other employers undertaking work onsite.

The role
You will be responsible for:
  • Conducting site inspections, audits and spot checks across construction and operational activities
  • Monitoring high-risk construction activities and escalating safety concerns where required
  • Reviewing and verifying SWMS, permits and other relevant safety documentation
  • Providing advice on construction risk management and safe work practices
  • Supporting the implementation and adoption of OHS systems and processes
  • Identifying existing and emerging hazards and supporting corrective and preventative actions
  • Supporting incident investigations, inspections and reporting
  • Monitoring corrective actions and ensuring appropriate follow-through
  • Working closely with project, automation, safety, contractor and site leadership teams
  • Supporting safety initiatives and continual improvement activities
  • Coaching and influencing contractors, leaders and operational teams to strengthen safety behaviours
  • Supporting OHS compliance, reporting, data analysis and performance tracking
  • Preparing safety reports, metrics and KPIs for leadership and project stakeholders
  • Liaising with regulators and external stakeholders where required
  • Attending toolbox talks and site meetings as required
About youTo be successful, you will ideally bring:
  • Previous experience as an OHS / Safety Advisor within construction, major projects or another high-risk environment
  • Strong experience working across multi-contractor construction sites
  • A background in contractor safety management and safety assurance
  • Strong knowledge of Victorian OHS legislation, regulatory requirements and industry standards
  • Experience reviewing SWMS and other high-risk construction documentation
  • Experience supporting incident investigations and corrective actions
  • Confidence engaging with contractors, supervisors, site managers and senior stakeholders
  • Strong coaching, influencing and relationship-building skills
  • The ability to work independently, identify issues and proactively drive outcomes
  • Strong reporting, documentation and Microsoft Office skills

Qualifications
Ideally you will hold:
  • Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety or higher
  • ICAM investigation training or similar
  • Current Construction White Card
  • Current CPR and First Aid qualifications

The details
  • Rate: $966 per day inclusive of super
  • Location: Truganina, VIC
  • Contract: Initial 12 months, with the approved project duration currently extending to approximately April 2028
  • Hours: Full-time, with site operating hours generally between 6:00am and 4:00pm
  • Onsite requirement: Approximately 3 days per week onsite
  • Large-scale construction environment with significant contractor and operational interfaces

This is a strong opportunity for an experienced construction safety professional who enjoys being visible onsite, working collaboratively with multiple stakeholders and providing practical, credible safety assurance across a complex project environment.

job.title: Fixed Plant Electrician
job.description:
Fixed Plant Maintenance Electrician FIFO Perth | 8:6 / 7:7 Roster | Various Iron Ore Sites Across the Pilbara
Are you an experienced Fixed Plant Maintenance Electrician looking for your next FIFO opportunity with a leading mining contractor supporting multiple major iron ore operations across the Pilbara?
We are currently seeking skilled and safety-focused Electricians for ongoing assignments across a range of iron ore sites. These positions offer a family-friendly 8:6 / 7:7 days and nights roster, competitive rates, and long-term career opportunities with immediate starts available.

The Opportunity As a member of the Maintenance team, you will play a critical role in maintaining the reliability, availability, and performance of fixed plant assets within a high-performing mining environment.
Key Responsibilities
  • Carry out preventative, breakdown, and corrective maintenance on fixed plant equipment
  • Diagnose and fault-find electrical issues across processing infrastructure
  • Maintain crushers, conveyors, screens, pumps, stackers, reclaimers, and associated plant equipment
  • Execute maintenance activities in accordance with site procedures and safety requirements
  • Complete inspections, testing, and maintenance documentation
  • Work collaboratively with Operations and Maintenance teams to maximise plant uptime
About You To be successful, you will have:
  • WA Electrical Workers Licence
  • Current Australian Driver's Licence
  • Demonstrated fixed plant maintenance experience within mining, resources, or heavy industry
  • Strong fault-finding and troubleshooting skills
  • Ability to work autonomously and within a team environment
  • Strong commitment to safety and site compliance
Highly Regarded
  • Iron ore processing plant experience
  • PLC and industrial control systems experience
  • HV Switching qualification
  • Working at Heights and Confined Space certifications
  • Instrumentation experience
What's On Offer?
  • FIFO from Perth
  • 8:6 / 7:7 day and night roster
  • Opportunities across multiple iron ore operations throughout the Pilbara
  • Competitive hourly rates
  • Long-term and ongoing work opportunities
  • Immediate starts available
  • Strong safety culture and supportive site teams
  • Opportunity to work with some of Australia's leading mining operations
Apply Now If you're an experienced Fixed Plant Maintenance Electrician seeking your next FIFO opportunity across Western Australia's premier iron ore operations, we want to hear from you.
Apply today with your updated resume or contact our team for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Branch Manager
job.description:
Branch Manager | Canberra | FMCG & Distribution

Permanent | Full time

$165,000 – $175,000 + super | STI | Fully Maintained Company Vehicle
  • Senior leadership opportunity within a well-established national business
  • Lead a 50–60 person branch operation
  • Responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse and customer service
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Branch Manager to take overall responsibility for a large and established distribution operation in Canberra.

This is a senior leadership position with responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse, administration and customer service, with a strong focus on branch profitability, customer service and team performance.

Reporting to senior management, you'll lead a team of approximately 50–60 employees and work closely with an experienced leadership group across the branch.

This is an opportunity for a confident and commercially minded leader to take ownership of an established operation, drive performance and identify opportunities to improve the way the business operates.

About the Role

You'll be responsible for:
  • Leading the day-to-day operations of the branch across sales, warehouse, transport and administration.
  • Delivering budgeted EBIT, revenue and profitability targets.
  • Managing branch budgets, forecasts, costs and financial performance.
  • Analysing P&L results and operational KPIs and taking corrective action where required.
  • Leading and developing a team of approximately 50–60 employees.
  • Driving customer growth, retention and service excellence.
  • Building strong relationships with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Managing inventory and ensuring customer demand is supported effectively.
  • Identifying new business opportunities and opportunities for growth.
  • Improving productivity, processes and operational efficiency.
  • Ensuring high standards of WHS, food safety, HACCP and Chain of Responsibility compliance.
  • Creating a culture of accountability, teamwork and continuous improvement.
  • Making timely decisions and providing clear direction across the branch.
About You

We're looking for an experienced operational leader who combines commercial understanding with strong people and operational leadership.

You'll ideally have:
  • Previous experience as a Branch Manager, Operations Manager, Distribution Manager, General Manager or similar.
  • Experience managing a sizeable workforce and multiple operational functions.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to interpret P&L, budgets and financial performance.
  • Experience managing costs, productivity and operational KPIs.
  • Strong customer relationship and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making ability.
  • A visible, hands-on leadership style.
  • The confidence to challenge existing processes and drive positive change.
  • Strong communication and people management skills.
  • The ability to perform in a fast-paced, operational environment.
Experience in these areas will be highly regarded:
  • FMCG
  • Food distribution or foodservice
  • Grocery or wholesale distribution
  • Transport and logistics
  • Warehouse and distribution
  • High-volume operational environments
  • HACCP and food safety
  • Chain of Responsibility
  • WHS and psychosocial safety
Forklift or heavy vehicle licences are advantageous but not essential.

The Leadership Opportunity

This role will suit someone who enjoys being close to the operation and isn't afraid to make decisions.

You'll be taking over an established operation with experienced people and established ways of working.

The opportunity is to build on what's working, identify what can be improved and lead the team through positive change.

We're looking for someone who:
  • Takes ownership
  • Leads from the front
  • Makes decisions
  • Holds people accountable
  • Develops and supports their team
  • Builds strong customer relationships
  • Looks for better ways of doing things
  • Can balance people, customers and commercial outcomes
What's on Offer
  • $165,000 – $175,000 + super
  • Fully maintained company vehicle
  • STI / incentive program
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
  • Staff discounts and additional benefits
  • Opportunity to lead a substantial operation within an established national business
  • Genuine scope to influence operational performance and branch growth
Apply Now

If you're an experienced Branch or Operations Manager looking for a role where you can take genuine ownership and make a measurable impact, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply now with your updated resume and cover letter.

Early applications are encouraged, as shortlisting may commence before the closing date of Friday 2 October 2026.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. All applications will be treated confidentially.

As part of the recruitment process, successful candidates may be required to complete employment checks, which may include a medical assessment, drug and alcohol testing, National Police History Check and licence validation.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.
